plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/20820
Crypto-theft coding convention used throughout this batch: stolen funds coded as confidentiality data variety Virtual currency (data_victim Victim organization unless customer wallets were drained), integrity Fraudulent transaction for the unauthorized transfers, and the USD loss in impact (Asset and fraud). No template tag; coded as Hacking-ext-unknown with S - Unknown/vector Unknown. Actor: CEO says the evidence points to a North Korea-linked group -> Nation-state KP (victim's own attribution). Data: 1,590 in-app wallets (their keys) -> Credentials (1,590 is a wallet count, so no amount/data_total); drained funds -> Virtual currency (amount stolen not disclosed). Availability Interruption (app shut down). Victim country/headcount Unknown; NAICS 513210 (app publisher). dbir_year 2025.

summary: On June 22, 2024 crypto portfolio tracker CoinStats was breached and about 1,590 wallets created within the app (about 1.3% of CoinStats wallets) were affected; connected wallets and exchange accounts were not. CEO Narek Gevorgyan said evidence pointed to a group with North Korean connections. CoinStats shut down the app and told affected users to move funds using their exported private keys.
